refuted.file_line: crates/store/src/canonical.rs:30474 (only the census note's 'writer could stay FK-OFF' hazard)
refuted.why: The leak itself stands. The FK-OFF consequence does not: turso_core 0.7.2 translate/pragma.rs:701-704 calls connection.set_foreign_keys_enabled(enabled) whether or not a transaction is open, so `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` at canonical.rs:30460 still takes effect inside a dangling transaction.

refuted.file_line: (general qualifier on every COMMIT-only leak, none fully refuted)
refuted.why: No leaks=true site turns out safe: each one really issues no ROLLBACK on the path named. How reachable the COMMIT-only leaks are depends on the engine, though. In op_auto_commit, turso sets auto_commit=true before commit_txn, so an I/O or disk-full error during the actual commit leaves is_autocommit()==true, and a ROLLBACK then answers 'cannot rollback - no transaction is active'. The open-transaction outcome on COMMIT needs check_deferred_fk_on_commit (the schema has no DEFERRABLE FKs, so this cannot happen today), StatementsInProgress, or a poisoned transaction, which turso rolls back itself. Body-path leaks are more reachable: apply_tenders flush, the build_plan_groups/link_step loops, rates, merge_provisional, insert_legacy_ojs_keys and backfill_org_name_norm. Constraint and FK errors, and any error in a multi-row or REPLACE write, roll back only the statement (vdbe/mod.rs abort). A generic error on a single-row write or a read inside BEGIN, by contrast, makes turso roll back the WHOLE transaction (the TxnCleanup::None arm). So the issue's 'turso aborts only the failing statement' is true for constraint errors and journaled writes, but not universally.

I re-read 9571, 10104, 11598, 11651, 11991, 13589, 16188, 17081, 18245, 18500, 21102, 23203, 29203 and lib.rs:2533, and checked the head of every other BEGIN site (19151, 19809, 20913, 21138, 21192, 21252, 21532, 21668, 21896, 23025, 23725, 23807, 24008, 24251, 24471, 24673, 25696, 26170, 26217, 27407, 22555). All are safe as the census says. Every `?` sits inside the async block or a finish_tx body, and every early return (dry_run, parity aborts, stop()) comes before BEGIN or exits through the commit. A heuristic scan for top-level `?`/`return` between each BEGIN and its COMMIT found nothing new.

Not a BEGIN literal, but the same wedge: a PANIC between BEGIN and COMMIT drops the MutexGuard with the transaction open. Examples are the `.expect()` calls at canonical.rs:17094/17099 and any unwrap inside a body. Async Drop does not exist, so no helper can ROLLBACK here.

Not a BEGIN literal, but the same wedge: a dropped future can leave the transaction open. If a writer future is cancelled while it holds the guard mid-transaction, turso marks the transaction poisoned but leaves it open. The request-scoped callers run inline in HTTP handler futures: admin.rs:151/317/407/497/565/610 (record_*) and the account delete (accounts.rs:271). The /v1 deadline layer (v1/mod.rs:681, REQUEST_DEADLINE 30s) does not wrap /admin (main.rs:81-82). Exposure is therefore a client disconnect or HTTP/2 reset, not the timeout. supervisor.rs:1200 persist_queued wraps a job-row persist in a 30s timeout, but that persist is an autocommit write with no BEGIN.

Test, probe and example only, not production: plain `BEGIN` in crates/store/tests/*.rs (about 25 files, e.g. r2_merge.rs:114, r3_merge.rs:75, placeholder_dissolve.rs:27), the BEGIN IMMEDIATE in mention_fk_probe.rs:169 and turso_temp_db_leak.rs:110/122/128, crates/store/examples/crash_probe.rs:83, and reader BEGINs in checkpoint.rs:236/305 (#[cfg(test)]). There are no SAVEPOINTs, no `.transaction()` API use, and no BEGIN in execute_batch schema strings. crates/app and crates/ingest have no BEGIN/COMMIT literals.
